prompt:
Write a police officer's crash report narrative (about 150 words). Collision type: low-speed head-on collision in Katy, Texas. The claimant was a driver and reported back strain. Refer to people as Driver 1, Driver 2 or Passenger. No names, no dates. (Internal reference C-1230; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The reported injury is plausible for a crash like this one.
- Photos confirm some details, but there are no independent witnesses.
- The vehicle damage matches the described impact.
- The police and witnesses confirm the claimant was in the vehicle.
- No earlier damage to the vehicle is known.
- The driver is named on the policy.
text: Officers were dispatched to a two-vehicle collision on a roadway in Katy, Texas, where the vehicles had come together in a low-speed head-on impact. Driver 1 was operating the first vehicle and Driver 2 the second. Driver 1 stated that the force of the impact caused immediate discomfort and that a lower back strain developed shortly afterward, consistent with the mechanics of a collision of this type. Responding officers observed visible front-end damage to both vehicles, and the damage pattern on the first vehicle appeared consistent with the described point of impact. No prior damage to the vehicle was known to the reporting parties or identified during the inspection. Photographs taken at the scene corroborate several of the reported details. No independent witnesses were located. Officers confirmed through statements from both drivers and from the scene that the Passenger was seated in the first vehicle at the time of the collision. Driver 1 is listed as a named insured on the policy covering that vehicle, which was verified at the scene.
